argument: I verified the entry mechanics with my own tools before opining: EWG/EFA pair-ratio prints 0.4055, 16.7th percentile of the 52-wk range (0.3945-0.4778), z-score -1.01 as of 2026-08-07 — the proposal's numbers check out exactly. Technical scan on EWG is outright constructive: price above the 20/50/100/200-day SMAs, golden cross in place, MACD positive and widening, overall score 8/10 bullish. So the 'confirmed inflection, not the knife' framing is defensible — momentum is with the trade even though the ratio sits near the bottom of its range. Two honest caveats from the data. First, 63-day relative strength vs EFA is still marginally negative (-0.78%), so the ratio turn is barely a month old; the 'confirmation' is thin, and the Aug 21 flash PMI is a genuinely binary checkpoint given the stop at 0.3954 is only a ~1-sigma reversion away (z -1.01 means a fresh low is well inside the distribution). Second, absolute-price RSI at 68.6 means you are not buying an absolute dip — this is a relative-value mean-reversion entry with absolute momentum already extended, which is fine but means the entry timing carries less margin for error than the 17th-percentile framing suggests. From my own coverage vantage, the sector read-through is mildly supportive rather than contradictory: EWG's comm-services exposure is essentially Deutsche Telekom, a domestic-demand beneficiary of the fiscal impulse, and a German industrial recovery is a modest tailwind for European ad budgets, which matter to META/GOOG European revenue (~a quarter of the total) — nothing in my sleeve argues against the thesis. The strongest part of the pitch is the crowding asymmetry (periphery at the 96th percentile while Germany sits at the 17th); the weakest is that two event risks (Aug 21 PMI, ~Sep 10 ECB) sit inside the stop's noise band, so position sizing should respect that the stop may get tested by data variance rather than thesis failure. Net: support at the proposed conviction of 7.
